title: Safety after a register update
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $x,v$ be Boolean words, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $v$. Choose a natural-number index $i$, a phase $\mathrm{ph}$, a program state $\ell$, a tape content $f:\mathbb Z\to\{\text{blank},0,1\}$, and a head position $p\in\mathbb Z$. Suppose every original work-tape head of $c$ lies in $[-S,S]$, the program has no oracle call at state $\ell$, and $-1\le p\le |\mathrm{bits}(|v|+1)|$. Replace the extra tape of the encoded configuration by $f$ with its head at $p$, and set its state to $\ell$. The resulting configuration satisfies the safety bounds for input length $|v|$ and parameter $S$.
